utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Good afternoon to you, sir. Could you remind you the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours just very briefly before I continue with my questioning, yesterday during the witness direct examination I rose about a particular issue where I stated I hadn't received adequate notice of that issue being raised. I haven't had the chance to review my materials last night I can see that I was mistaken. These issues were touched on and you just wanted to make that clear for the Trial Chamber and also to offer my apologies to my colleague Mr. Apostolski for yesterday's interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that is correct Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanovski, I would like to continue with our questioning and I'd like to touch now on the topic of the mine incident at Ljubotenski Bacila. And you gave some description of this yesterday, and if I can just recap a part of that. I believe you said that you were having your breakfast at the children's rest house when you were told about the mine incident. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this was about 8.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And I believe you testified you drove part of the way to Ljubotenski Bacila and then walked the rest. Could you explain why you only drove part of the way?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My driver was driving the jeep, and we were driving until we were in the area of our check-points. When we passed them, we stopped and we continued on foot, because we could hear firing from Ljubotenski Bacila, and we had to be cautious and to go there on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And so even having driven part of the way, it took you an hour to get there from -- from your post at the children's rest house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the rest house to Ljubotenski Bacila, it took us about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this would be consistent with what you testified yesterday about the distance between the Ljubanci-Ljuboten area and Ljubotenski Bacila with the winding mountain roads. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a winding road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now when you arrived at Ljubotenski Bacila, was the fighting still under way there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The fighting was still under way. As I explained yesterday, they were in the area of Ardievi Bacila.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And did you have a good view of what was going on there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the place of the explosion, I could only see where the fire was coming from and to see Ardievi Bacila as a place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: You described yesterday seeing a combat helicopter in the area. Could you tell us what that combat helicopter was doing?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The combat helicopter was opening fire around the forest near the sheepfolds. For a few minute, it was opening fire towards the forest around the sheepfolds and towards Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you've described shooting coming from the area of Ardievi Bacila. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. At the moment when we got there, the fire was coming from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could we please show 65 ter 1231, and this is in tab 5 also of the binder we provided. And actually I believe this may have been admitted yesterday, P595.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is what I wished to assist my learned colleague with. This is Exhibit P595.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanovski, if you look at the bottom of the map there, the map that you saw earlier, you'll see the words Ardievi Bacila with an arrow going to an area north of the site of the explosion. Did you make that marking on the map?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this is the position where you saw the fire coming from. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the direction from which our positions were shooting and from where shots could be heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the shots could be heard from Ardievi Bacila. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They could be heard from Ardievi Bacila.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And as we can see from this map, that position is in the opposite direction from Ljuboten village, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, if we look at the map and your marking on it, can you see the site of the explosion at Ljubotenski Bacila, can you see Ljuboten village to the south, to the south-west, perhaps, and Ardievi Bacila, as you've marked it, is up to the north. So it is in the opposite direction, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the map, it is so. However, from Ardievi Bacila, one cannot see the village of Ljuboten, nor from the place where the truck exploded. One cannot see the village Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on from there also. Now, can I just ask you, did you personally see any of the attackers in that area withdrawing towards Ljuboten village?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any attackers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And following the mine incident, once the situation had calmed down, did you return to Smok at that point?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I explained yesterday, sometime after 1.00, I returned to Smok.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And is it correct, Mr. Grozdanovski, that two members of your unit were on the truck that was hit by the mine, or the truck that hit the mine?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did those members receive any injuries?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were both wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move on to the evening of Friday, the 10 the August. And that evening, didn't you attend a meeting at the command headquarters in the Ljubanci school?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All commanders of companies were present together with the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So Major Despodov, being the commander, is that right, he was there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was chairing the meeting, Major Despodov Mitre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And Mario Jurisic was also at this meeting, was he?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Are you able to recall whether any members of the Ministry of Interior, or any police, were present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: But you do recall at least, don't you, that there were police officers in the school yard at that time. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And those police officers were wearing camouflage uniforms with police insignia on them?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were in police camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And there also police vehicles there in the yard. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And didn't these police also have boxes that you believe contained fire-arms?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two boxes, but I do not know what was in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, do you recall telling the interviewer from the Office of the Prosecutor during your suspect interview that these boxes were the same shape, size and colour of boxes that the army used to transport or to carry weapons in?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Such were the boxes. But we use those boxes for other purposes, for protective wear, for eating utensils. So unless I looked into them and saw what was in them, I could not say what was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of these police, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did you get a sense of the mood amongst these police after the mine incident?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say. They were standing there. I came with my vehicle, and I immediately entered to see the commander. Therefore, I could not get a sense of the mood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you're certain when you say that you didn't speak to any of these police at that time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: During your second suspect interview on the 8th of November, 2004, do you recall being shown some photo boards?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall being warned that you should only make an identification if you're certain that you recognise a particular person?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you also recall being told that the suspect might not be on the photo board at all.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment, I could not recall, but perhaps they did tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, if we could please show 65 ter 1233. And this is also in tab 20 of the witness binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Grozdanovski, do you have that in front of you at the moment?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, do you recall being shown this photo board at your suspect interview?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And in your own language, could you please read to us the line that's handwritten at the top?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I have not seen these photograph previously."

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, there are circles around the numbers 7 and 8, and there's something written under those numbers. Could you please read that to us?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It writes: "I think I saw them in the school courtyard in the village of Ljubanci on the 10th of August, 2001."

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And is that your signature underneath that, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And then can you see under that is written: "Identification done 8 November 2004 in the presence, Kuehnel Thomas investigator OTP, Grozdanovski Nikolce, suspect." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I seek to tender 65 ter 1233.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P597, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Grozdanovski, do you remember giving your telephone number to any of these policemen who were in the school courtyard?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not give my telephone to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did any of these policemen give you their telephone numbers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Perhaps I will be a bit more specific here. Isn't it true, Mr. Grozdanovski, that in fact you swapped telephone numbers with Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And isn't it true, Mr. Grozdanovski, that Johan Tarculovski actually attended that meeting in the school building?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. When I was present in the building, Johan Tarculovski or anyone else was not present at the meeting, except persons from the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'll move on, Mr. Grozdanovski, now to the events of Saturday, the 11th of August. And isn't it true that you spent that night, Saturday, the 11th of August, at the children's rest house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did you stay there the whole night?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the whole night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Mario Jurisic's unit was also housed at the rest house, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And Mario Jurisic himself was there on the night of August the 11th, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanovski, Mario Jurisic testified before this Tribunal. And before I go on to the subject of his testimony, I'd like to ask you, did you see any police staying over at the children's rest house on the night of Saturday, the 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, as I said, Mr. Jurisic testified before this Tribunal on the 5th of July, 2007, and for reference this is at transcript pages 3300 to 3302. And, Mr. Grozdanovski, he said when he was asked whether anyone besides his unit and yours had stayed in the rest house on that night that there was group of around ten policemen they were wearing camouflage uniforms with police emblems. They were also wearing bullet proof vests, and they were armed with pistols and automatic rifles. He further said they arrived in the evening in a police car and a truck, and that he had been informed in advance that these police would be staying at the rest house that night. And furthermore, Mr. Grozdanovski, he identified Johan Tarculovski as being one of those individuals who spent that night there. And before I ask you to comment on that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could please show exhibit P303 which is also in tab 9 of the binders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you saw this document yesterday, Mr. Grozdanovski. This is a Official Note prepared by Captain Ljupco Kostadinov. And could I please ask you to turn to page 2 in the top of the page. And you will see that it states here that the persons that arrived in the area of the 3rd Guardist Battalion referring to the policemen were accommodated in the mountain lodge in the village Ljubanci, and some of them, also in private houses, and they spent the night there. Do you see that, Mr. Grozdanovski? This should be the very first paragraph on the second page, Mr. Grozdanovski.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Are you in tab 9 there, Mr. Grozdanovski.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The same page is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, I'll move on from there, Mr. Grozdanovski. Can I just ask you, then, in light of the testimony of Mario Jurisic, does that refresh your recollection as to whether any police officers stayed at the rest house on the night of the 11th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain the system of activities in our battalion. Mario, as the commander of the 1st Company, had the duty to lead or to be in charge of the children's rest house. That means to accommodate soldiers, to provide for the food, everything regarding the cooks, the eating was under his charge. I had no obligations there. I had received premises to accommodate my soldiers and no more than that. I had no activities regarding procuring food or other equipment. This was all in the charge of Mario. If soldiers or if others, police officers, as you say, came then commander Mitre told Mario, gave him the duties, and he accommodated them. I don't recall, I don't remember having seen police officer that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So can I take it from what you said that police officers may well have been there. You simply yourself did not see them?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now before the events in Ljuboten that weekend of the 10th to the 12th of August, had you ever met Johan Tarculovski yourself?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did you know him at all?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: But isn't that correct we have seen from the photo board you were just shown that you have recognised him as a policeman who you saw in the school yard in Ljubanci on the 10th of August?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may seen on that photograph that although they told me to circle one person, I circled two, because I wasn't sure. I first met and recognised Johan Tarculovski from television. When I saw him on television, I recognised him, and I recognised him on the photographs; but I wasn't sure, and there is why I circled two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: In the note you made on the photo board you didn't say there that you weren't sure, did you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If reads "I think it is the person so-and-so." This is what is written on the photo board. Even then I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, did you have a mobile phone at this time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall what your telephone number was for that mobile phone?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you please tell us that telephone number?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can this be done privately? I don't want to issue ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Grozdanovski, didn't you also testify that at the time the shooting started -- at the time you got to the check-point at Smok, you were just observing because there was no fire directed at your positions at that point. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at some later point fire was directed against your positions and you then responded with mortar fire. And you did not see members of the police forces down in the village until much later, sometime after 9.00 a.m. Do you recall testifying to that effect?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you then testified that when you saw the police near one of the targets you stopped firing in that direction and targeted another area. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you also described watching the police advance through the village behind a Hermelin until eventually you stopped firing when they got to the area near the mosque. Is that also an accurate summary of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. More or less, we took the mosque as our spot. But it was above the mosque on the road towards Rastak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Grozdanovski, isn't it true that the version of events that you described yesterday here in this Court is very different to the version that you gave to the interviewers from the Office of the Prosecutor during your suspect interviews?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I'm speaking about the events as they went on. Whether there are some small difference about the time or not. Even then I said that I cannot really define the time accurately. If you see the document, you will see that is the only weak spot because I cannot guarantee about the accurate time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Wouldn't you agree that when being interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor back in 2004 your recollection of events would have been much fresher in your mind than it is today?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollections were the freshest on the 13th, when I made my first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I would like to ask you a few questions about what you said about the time the action started, and the time that you saw the police. And I would ask to you turn to tab 2. This is 65 ter number 1228. And this is your first suspect interview from 30th of July, 2004. And do you have the portion that has been translated into Macedonian in front of you, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could go to page 24 of the Macedonian translation and page 51 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And approximately halfway down the page, or perhaps it's a bit further down from that. And you are were asked the question: "Okay so just tell us please in your own words thoughts an overview what happened on Sunday, 12th August, the time of the events, what can you remember. You see your answer is: "I don't remember the precise time whether it was 6.00 or 6.15. We heard shots and Major Despodov but don't take my word for it, although I think it was Major Despodov orders us to go to the positions, and I left to the positions at Smok with three to four soldiers of mine, communication men and scouts, et cetera. And then you continue on: "And until 8.00, I know that approximately around 8.00 the police was firing there in the village, against the villagers. You were then asked to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: You stated: "The Ljuboten villagers shot at the police, and the police shot at them. And you were asked: "Okay, did you monitor that. You replied yes and then you said yes you can see everything nicely. Until 8.00 we were not fired at, the army. Did you follow that, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And would you agree that this is very different to what you said here in the court yesterday?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was explaining the times, as I mentioned just earlier, and then also when my hearing was finished, at the end, I made the comment that I cannot guarantee the accuracy of the times. Just a while back, I said that my best recollection of the 13th of August was when I wrote my first statement. Here, one hour later, or sooner, I don't know why I said this. This is what I recalled at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, do you also recall saying yesterday that the police did not enter the village until much later, that when you first got to the observation point you didn't see any police there. There was just shooting going on from the villagers. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall here I say and when I was saying this, I probably meant that there were shooting at someone. That someone was probably the police. Because there was a police check-point in Ljuboten where the Macedonian houses were. If they were opening fire my presumption was that they were firing at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Grozdanovski, from your statement, it doesn't appear to be a presumption because you specifically state that the police that were in the village, the police were firing there in the village, and you even say: Yes, you can see everything nicely. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I explained, there was a police check-point at the beginning of the village of Ljuboten. And when we were looking at the terrorists shooting at the check-point, and there was fire from the check-point towards the terrorists. This is the fire I was thinking of. The police could not have been seen because, at that time, in August, the trees are in bloom and they cannot be seen until -- unless they're standing out in the open. For the first time, I saw them when they came to the carabine near the orthodox church, which I encircled yesterday, because here it is an empty area, and it is possible to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, would you simply agree that what you said in your suspect statement is something different.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained this. I don't see how it's different. It was just that I presumed that there were shooting at the police check-point. They had to be shooting at someone. In that direction there was a police check-point. After, it came that my presumption was true because we saw the police officers and this is why when I was explaining I said that they were shooting towards the police because later I found out that they were shooting policemen and this is what I knew. What I was explaining yesterday was a chronological line of events.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move on and now I'd like to ask you some questions about the mortars, the mortar shells that you described observing falling in an area close to the orthodox church. And for reference, this is at page 10417 of the transcript from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we could please -- if we could bring up Exhibit 2D87.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, do you remember seeing this map yesterday, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And on it with the number 1, you marked the orthodox church, right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And a little way to the right, you marked an area where you said shells fell that had been fired apparently by the NLA. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, you didn't mention these mortar shells at all during your suspect interviews, did you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment I wasn't asked about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Grozdanovski, you were being interviewed as a suspect. Didn't you think that this information might have been to your benefit, if you had told this to the interviewers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One cannot remember all details at that moment. Later on, when I thought about this, I recalled this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could we -- if we could be shown Exhibit 1D281.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And it is on the screen in front of you, Mr. Grozdanovski, and if-- sorry, that's fine there. Now, you were shown this particular photograph, this panoramic photograph of Ljuboten on two separate occasions, right, you were shown it on the 30th of July and the 8th of November, 2004. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you were given two chances, four months apart, to make any relevant annotations that you thought about on this map. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, at that time I did not recall this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I would ask that Exhibit 1D281.3 be shown now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanovski, this is another panoramic photo of Ljuboten. It's a better view actually of the right side of the first panorama that we just looked at. And if you look in the photo towards the centre do you see the orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you see the annotation you made C-1, three to four terrorists.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And in the house where the line goes to, you've written in white, four to six. And that means that you fired four to six mortar shells in that direction, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is how I remembered at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: As you've said, you haven't made any markings there showing where these alleged shells from the NLA landed, have you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shells are not mine. I only mark the shells that were fired from my mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: You've said on at least a couple of occasions so far that your best recollection of the events came on the 13th of August. So could I ask you to turn to tab 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this is Exhibit 1D25.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Grozdanovski, do you recognise this as the report that you wrote, about the events in Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And anywhere in this report does it make any mention of the NLA shells landing in that area to the right of the area of the orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained yesterday that Major Despodov wanted us to explain which were the targets that we fired at on the 12th, and in my statement I just paid attention to those moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So your answer would be, no, there's no mention of these shells from the NLA in this report?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're not mentioned because, at the time, they were not firing at our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on. If you could now turn to tab 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this is Exhibit 1D12. And, Your Honours, there is a page missing from the court binder. It's the last page of the Macedonian translation, and we do have additional hard copies here, if we could distribute those at the moment, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanovski, you will see that this is an investigator's note of an interview with Henry Bolton, who is an OSCE monitor. If you turn to page 2, and you'll see the second from bottom paragraph, there's a paragraph starting: "On Sunday, 12/8/02. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this reads: "On Sunday 12/08/02, HB was together with VC shared accommodation. About 0800 and 0805 hours he heard a loud detonation and saw a large plume of smoke rising from a location that appeared to be near the orthodox church in the village of Ljuboten. Both he and VC believed that this detonation was the result of a heavy mortar probably of 120-millimetre calibre. About five minutes later, two more similar loud denotations were heard and plumes of smoke were visible. HB was of the opinion that these were also caused by heavy mortar fire, 120-millimetre. I fell about 150 to 200 metres away from the first point of impact. The direction was in the direction of the orthodox church but closer to it. Soon after, uncertain of the type lapse the Macedonian army post located above the village of Ljuboten fired at Salvo of mortar fire directed at the upper part of Ljuboten village, 80-millimetre medium mortars. HB estimated that the number of rounds that fell on that part of the village to have been in the region of 50 to 60." Did you follow that, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, if you go to the last page under the heading: Opinion of HB. That states: "HB stated that he was aware that there was a police post near the church which was permanently manned by about ten reservist Macedonian police. He believed there was a possibility that the police post was the target. He argued that he believed from his own military experience that the first detonation was to establish range and direction whilst the second and third was send as corrected fire. There were no Albanians in the direction that the rounds fell. The only logical target could have been the Macedonian police post. HB did not believe that the Macedonian forces, in and around the area, had 120-millimetre mortars at their disposal. He felt that the NLA were attacking the police post. He had nothing to support this belief. He was basing his opinion on his military and local experience." Did you follow that, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So can you see that his belief was that the first explosions were 120-millimetre mortars, and he believe they were fired by the NLA. Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And then he apparently also believed that the army of Macedonia responded with 80-millimetre mortars, did you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: But in fact the army did have 120-millimetre mortars in the area, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And also there were ethnic Albanians in the area around the orthodox church, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So the facts that he relied upon to make this particular conclusion that the NLA fired the first mortar rounds into the village are flawed, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now when I look at this, I can give my opinion. Obviously HB, when he was saying this, he mixed up the facts, because first he says 120-millimetres and then he says 80. Probably it was the other way around. Probably he saw the 80 millimetres first and then 120-millimetre. Because the shells that he is talking about later are 120-millimetres, while in this document he says they were 80 millimetres. So obviously he mixed it up, because we fire 82-millimetre shell first and then fired 120-millimetres shells because that what is we were saying all the time that we were firing at the terrorists with 120-millimetre shells because here in this document he mixes the two of them. Obviously he mixed up the calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So I take it that with that you agree with me that there appears to be a flaw in his reasoning on this particular point.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I read just now, that is my conclusion. He made a mistake in the calibre of the mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Can we please now look at tab 41. This is Exhibit 1D24.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you'll see, Mr. Grozdanovski, that this is a special report by the OSCE on the Ljuboten incident and it is dated August 16th, 2001. Now, I would ask to you turn to page 3 of that document. And it's the second paragraph on that page in Macedonian, and in English it's the fourth paragraph and it reads: "On 12 August at 0805 hours the first mortar round fell on the village. It landed in the vicinity of the orthodox church in the Macedonian section of the village. Two more rounds followed, each closer to the church. All three are believed to have been 120-millimetre mortars. These are more likely to have been EAAG rounds than government and were the first shots fired in the village. Thereafter, the army fired on the Albanian side of the village with its smaller calibre mortars." Did you follow that, Mr. Grozdanovski? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And so it appears here that the same reasoning that Henry Bolton applied earlier has made it into this report, correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain this. If we follow this report, it turns out that the army didn't use 120-millimetres. It doesn't make any logic even to the hearing in Skopje, and yesterday I said that we were firing 120-millimetre shells. But if we only rely on this document it turns out that we only shelled 82-millimetre shells and we fired the first shells in Macedonian houses. It really doesn't make any logic, and I don't know how to explain this. Obviously he mixed up the calibre, because later we used 120-millimetre shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So perhaps if we can simplify this. Can I simply ask you, it is the case, isn't it, that you had 120-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you fired 120-millimetre mortar shells into an area close to the orthodox church.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the left side of the orthodox church, towards the Albanian houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could please look at Exhibit 2D91.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall being shown this photograph yesterday, Mr. Grozdanovski, and making the markings on it that we can see in front of us now?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you see the circle around the house with the number 2. You marked that as the location of the house you said machine-gun fire was coming from. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the morning of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you circled the house, labelled it with the number 3, and you said this marked a house where individuals were shooting from a balcony before running across to the house marked with number 2. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the house marked with the number 4 was a house that you had identified during your suspect interview and you say mistakenly identified as being the house where the machine-gun was located. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I encircled this house in Skopje, I circled it as target 3 that we targeted with the mortar shell. That was the house where the machine-gun was. Yesterday I apologise profoundly for making that mistake and for circling that house while I was having in mind house number 2, and this house was targeted with a 120-millimetre mortar shell because the machine-gun, that morning was in the house marked with number 3 and then it moved to the house marked with number 2. So when we were targeting house number 3, we were actually targeting house number 2, and I was sorry for making that mistake, because from the angle I mistook the house for the house number 4. I was really confused with this nylon on the field which was behind the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, if we could look at Exhibit 1D281. And this is also in tab 16 of your binder. And, Mr. Grozdanovski, you agree that you were shown this photograph on the 30th of July, 2004?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you circled a house and there's an arrow leading to it and underneath you've written the Macedonian word for "machine-gun," right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this is the house that you now say you were mistaken about. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could we now please go to tab 22, and if we could show 65 ter number 1235.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you'll see that this is the same photograph and that you were shown this photograph again four months later on the 8th of November, 2004. And, again, you marked that same house. Here you marked it with the number 3. Do you see that, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So four months later, when seeing this photo again, you still thought that this was the correct house, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I would kindly ask you to show me a photo that does not have circles, and if you show me that house you will see there's a nylon behind it and that nylon was so misleading for me, because I really don't know how to explain this to you. On the 12th, the house that we were targeting, there was a nylon behind it, just like there a nylon behind this house. And from this angle, this house looked like the one that we targeted. But then, when I looked the photo from the Smok position, then I saw the right house. If you have an empty or unmarked photo, you will see a nylon behind that house that was so misleading to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the time. Have I about five minutes left on this point. I wonder if I should carry on now or should we break now, and I can continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We would be happy to sit the five minutes if that's convenient. We'll be guided by you Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I will have this point finished in that time. As you've just said, Mr. Grozdanovski, the error came about because this picture was not taken from Smok. Well, I wonder if perhaps if you hold the hard copy in front of you --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And on the screen could we go back to 2D91, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Grozdanovski, you now have the two photographs in front of you. Wouldn't you agree that the panoramic photograph actually gives a much better perspective of the village of Ljuboten? Wouldn't it make it easier to locate the right house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The panoramic photo makes the house circled with number 2 far -- too far away from the position of Smok. And at the moment, it looked to me that that house was too remote and that we didn't target it with mortar shell. The panoramic photo shows that this house is at least one kilometre further away, but on this picture we can see how close these houses are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if we look at the photograph taken from Smok, wouldn't you agree that the house that you mistakenly identified in 2004 is on a rise?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not really a rise. I don't know how you see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, would you agree that the house you've marked with a number 2 is in something of a hollow or a dip in the field?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And yesterday you described seeing shooter firing from a balcony from one of a row of four houses and then running across to the other house where they fired from a hole in the roof. Now, did you make any mention of this particular fact in your suspect interviews with the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was only asked then what were the targets that I fired at, and I said that we were firing at this house only, because there was a machine-gun there. So when I fired our mortars, we were targeting only the target 2. So the interview was -- which was the house that we targeted, and yesterday I gave a broader picture of the events on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if we take that broader picture you provided yesterday, the house that you marked back in 2004, the house number 4 there, do you see anywhere by that a row of four houses with balconies?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house marked with number 4, I didn't say there were balcony there. I was talking about the house marked with number 3. The machine-gun was first in that house, and then it moved in the house now marked with number 2. For the house marked number 4, I don't think there were terrorists at that time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I understand that. What I'm asking you, Mr. Grozdanovski, is if you mistakenly identified house number 4 when you were intended to identify house number 2, how could you have made that mistake when there aren't four houses by that with balconies where these shooters would have run from?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were running away from the house marked with 2, and that happened in the end of the combat activities. In the end, when the police arrived to the house marked with number 3, the terrorists started to flee, and I targeted my target 3 sometime around 10.00, or I don't know what time exactly it was. I think it was around 10.00. Because after 10.30 we were not firing anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honour, I would seek to tender 65 ter 1235.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Which tab is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: That's tab 22. It's the photograph that was marked--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Your Honours, this would be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph will become Exhibit P598, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We resume now at 20 minutes past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanovski, at various times during your testimony yesterday you described the unit who went through the village of Ljuboten as either police, or as the security forces, or as soldiers. And I'd like to be clear about this now. Isn't it the case that the unit that you saw moving through Ljuboten was a police unit?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And yesterday you also testified quite extensively and in some detail about the movements of a Hermelin vehicle through the village. I'd just like to ask you why did you not mention this, why did you not describe this during your two suspect interviews?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't asked about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, again, Mr. Grozdanovski, you were being interviewed as a suspect. Didn't it occur to you that it would be in your interest to provide as full a picture as possible?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are all events that were not related to my unit. I described in more detail our activities as the army, as my unit. These were activities of the police, and this is why I did not elaborate on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, you were also shown a report yesterday that was prepared by Captain Ljupco Kostadinov, and you took issue with some aspects of this report. And so I would if we could perhaps pull up Exhibit P303, and this is also in tab 9. Do you have that report in front of you, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you can see that this is the report you were shown yesterday prepared by Captain Kostadinov. Now I'd like to ask you did you personally speak to Mr. Kostadinov on the 12th or the days thereafter?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If could you turn to page 2, please. About halfway down the page. Do you see a paragraph starting "On Sunday, 12/08/2001 at 0430 hours." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this states: "On Sunday, 12/08/2001 at 0430 hours the person Johan Tarculovski with the other persons MVR reservists started the action. Immediately after the start of the action Captain Nikolce Grozdanovski called up Major Despodov and informed him about the start of the action, which had been organised by MVR. "The reservists wearing MVR uniforms advanced in the village up arriving at the bridge where they there was a check-point and the house of a person Kenan. When they saw that they could not advance anymore, they called Major Despodov and they requested support for shooting at the mentioned buildings. Because the buildings were defended by machine-guns." And now can you please turn to page -- it's actually at the bottom of your page, Mr. Grozdanovski, and it is on page 3 in the English. And it is the last line in the Macedonian version. And it is approximately the third to last line in the English paragraph and it states: "During the support that was conducted by the 3rd Guardist Battalion to the MVR units by mortars 16 grenades of 120-millimetres were fired at which 13 in the village and three outside." Do you see that, Mr. Grozdanovski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: This information at least is correct, isn't it? You stated in your own report that you fired 16, 120-millimetre mortar shell, right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here this, what you read, the only thing true is that we fired 16 mortar shells. None of the other things are true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, at least in respect to this fact the source was reliable and accurate, the source of the information. Wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my statement also I said that we had fired 16 such shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Grozdanovski, at this point I'm just going to put some propositions to you. I'm not seeking a lengthy explanation on each point. I would simply like you to indicate whether or not you agree with the proposition that I'm putting to you. First of all wasn't it the case, Mr. Grozdanovski, that you were able to observe activities in and around the village of Ljuboten in the two months leading up to the events of the 10th to the 12th of August, 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you also agree that in that time had you no problems with the local population, and you personally saw nothing at that time to indicate a NLA presence in the village?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, do you agree that the testimony that you provided in court about these apparent indications of NLA presence are different to the information you provided during your suspect interviews?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you read yesterday to me about my statement, I also was saying that I was noticing some curious things going on in the village. The overall situation was good because there were no combat activities going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Grozdanovski, that you attended a meeting at the battalion headquarters in the school in Ljubanci on the 10th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And isn't it true that Johan Tarculovski and other members of the Ministry of Interior were also present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Commander Despodov Mitre was holding the meeting with us, only people from the army were present. All company commanders of the 3rd Guardist Battalion. There were no members of the MOI.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Mr. Grozdanovski, that around this time, you and Johan Tarculovski exchanged telephone numbers and you later had conversations regarding artillery support for the MOI operation in the village?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is absolutely not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Is it true that on the night of the 11th of August you were aware that Johan Tarculovski and other members of his MOI unit stayed overnight at the children's rest house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent the night at the children's rest house. As for where Johan Tarculovski spent the night, I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Grozdanovski, that on the morning of Sunday, the 12th of August, a police unit headed by Johan Tarculovski advanced into the village of Ljuboten and your mortar battery provided supportive fire for that police unit?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the police unit that were in the village are unknown to me. That we did fire over some matters that were shooting towards us, the army, this is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And I'm putting it to you, Mr. Grozdanovski, that the testimony that you've given to this Tribunal is very different to the information that you provided to the investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor during your suspect interviews. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree. Have you to point out to me which points I don't agree. Generally speaking like this, I believe it is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Grozdanovski, I put it to you that, here, testifying in front of the Tribunal, you have not been forthright and honest, and you have omitted certain details harmful to the accused and you have fabricated other details that help the accused. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which testimonies are beneficial and which are not. I answered to the question, and I spoke of the situation regarding the events of that period in the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness Nikolce Grozdanovski. I will have several additional questions for you. Do you recall yesterday when you were asked by the Prosecutor on page 10472 why you didn't say during the first interview anything about the bullets found along the road in the surrounds of Ljuboten in 2001. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recall the Prosecutor reading parts of your interview to you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at 65 ter 1228, which is at tab 2 of the Prosecution binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You can also look at this document on the screen. This is page 18 of both the Macedonian and English versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please scroll down a little bit in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: We have here TK asking you: "Did you see from your observation post any kind of activities that would indicate that there would be problems coming ahead like the results events of Ljuboten?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you see any kind of preparations for fighting, did you any preparations of fortifications, trench, bunkers, military positions, anything -- anything of this kind, and your answer is no?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this identical to your testimony before this Court, in the course of yesterday?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I emphasised that fortifications and combat activities were not seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Later you were asked any sort of typical preparations for fighting and your answer to that is no. And then TK asking you whether you saw any other signs of the presence of the NLA or its supporters, any sorts of flag or graffiti or other markings. And your answer to that was: "There were flags on the mosque but no other things." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you answered before this Court about the presence of the NLA in the village of Ljuboten or around Ljuboten, you did not mention this. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you explain to us why you did not mention this detail?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just as I said, the situation these days and this whole event might have had so many important details, but they're so numerous that I unintendedly omitted them. Yesterday I didn't mention the flag, but, yes, there was a flag on the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, there was a NLA flag but you did not mention this, and this is not on purpose?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this was not on purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were given the question to -- when you were answering the questions of the Prosecutor today about the time necessary for you to go from the rest house to Ljubotenski Bacila, you answered that you arrived there in about one hour's time, half an hour by car and half-hour by foot. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell us at what speed the vehicle was moving?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The car couldn't move faster than 20 to 30 kilometres per hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And when you left the vehicle, when you continued on foot, were you going at a quick pace? Were you moving slowly?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We tried to go faster, but we had bullet-proofs, ammunition, guns; and it was really hard to move on foot although we really wanted to get there as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. According to you, what is the normal time necessary to arrive from the children's rest house to Ljubotenski Bacila moving on foot?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: From the children's rest house to Ljubotenski Bacila.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you go on foot, at least an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And by car, how long would it be necessary to get there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 30 to 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And from Ljubotenski Bacila to Ljuboten, what is the time needed to get there on foot?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go downhill, maybe even faster, for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. You answered to the question of my learned colleague from the Prosecution that you saw terrorists only at Ardievi Bacila on the 10th of August, 2001, and you arrived at that site an hour later. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly request the witness to wait for the translation before he answers the question of the Defence attorney. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will attempt to avoid overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was it possible for terrorists to have been present in other areas hidden in the forest near Ljubotenski Bacila without you seeing them?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the most probable situation, because the terrorists, when they activated the mine, they were probably [as interpreted] the same terrorists that were in Ardievi Bacila. Those that were in Ardievi Bacila were probably terrorists that had been there to give them assistance. And later on, when there was a helicopter flying, they opened fire from several spots from the Ardievi Bacila towards Matejce. Obviously there were more terrorists around the forest.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, on in line 11, they were probably not the same terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recall yesterday's transcript page 1042 that you are shown a map and it was put to you that the Smok position is two kilometres away from the northern -- northeastern part of Ljuboten. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the map, P595.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this the map?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You also said that to the Prosecutor that when you were asked by the Prosecution, examined by the Prosecution, you confirmed this map. You verified this map as correct. In what sense did you verify this map?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sense of the points that mark the locations, and they may be correct, but not completely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are they absolutely correct, the points?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not absolutely correct. The point marking the Smok position is probably five millimetres further than marked on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And five millimetres on this map are quite significant.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes if the proportion is correct, yes, five millimetres is probably a lot. I guess the proportion here is 1: 10.000, so one millimetre means a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, when you said that this map was accurate, this was accuracy in terms where the positions were located.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But whether the point is in the correct spot, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: For example, you did not know, surely, about the positions of the NLA. I see here: NLA positions. That's generally speaking they were there but not precisely.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Generally they are okay, but whether they are accurate to the millimetre, I don't know. When I saw this map for the first time in Skopje I didn't really pay attention to each millimetre. But as locations, they are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could we try to maintain the pause between the questions and the answers, Witness. That way we can facilitate better interpretation. MR. APOSTOLSKI [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown photograph N003-7603. I might have gotten the number wrong. It's N005-7603.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know where this photograph was taken from?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is from the Ljubotenski Pat, towards Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, from the direction of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Can you see the Smok position on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see on this photograph the house in the northeastern part on the road towards Rastak, which you marked yesterday as houses from where shooting came from on the morning of the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark with a number 1 the position Smok and then mark the houses.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Position Smok is this one. Target 3 ...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You don't have to mark them all. You don't have to mark all targets. Can you erase the last thing you marked. Could you please mark the Smok position with the number 1?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the houses which you encircled with the number 2.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yesterday the Prosecution put it to you that this was a distance of two kilometres. Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think there's not more than 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D92, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Today when my learned colleague from the Prosecution was questioning you, you said that on the 10th of August, when you were at the meeting at the headquarters in the school, you saw police vehicles in the courtyard. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell us what type of vehicles these were. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think one of them was Lada jeep, and the other one was a passenger police vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you say "Lada," can you tell us more specifically, Lada jeep, what kind of jeep?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called them Lada Niva, and we used them as terrain vehicles. That's why we call them Lada jeep. Otherwise they're known as Lada Niva.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: After that you said you saw some boxes in the courtyard and that did you not know what was in those boxes. Did you know to whom those boxes belonged?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know whose they were. They were just in the yard. I didn't know who they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. On several occasions testifying before this Court, you said that the most accurate picture about the events in Ljuboten was your report prepared on the 13th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 1D24 -- my apologies, 2D31.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see this report in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct when I say that in this report you mentioned as a third target the new four houses, two in a row, there were machine-guns that were firing towards you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this in accordance with your testimony before this court.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I explained that in the beginning you will see the -- it says when I called the major, I explained the targets to him and the machine-gun was in that house; but later when we started fire the machine-gun was transported to another house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. And about this report the Prosecutor asked why you did not make mention of the three shells which you heard in the mornings. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: However, you also mentioned that at your positions around 11.00 other shells also fell, fired by the NLA from Meckan Kamen?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this report also does not contain the mention of these shells?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Why didn't you mention these shells which fell from Bel Kamen?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said on several occasions that the report was written just to describe the targets and the events in Ljuboten, not for the other happenings that day. So, in this report, I was supposed to write just about the targets that I identified and what my reaction was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Also, the Prosecutor put it to you that you did not mention the right time during the hearing of the investigator during your interviews in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That Prosecutor suggested that this was in fact 6.00 and that this was a great omission on your part. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the report which you gave immediately after the events, does it say that on the 12th of August, 2001, in the morning, I was in the rest house carrying out my regular duties and around 8.00 we heard several long bursts of fire which kept repeating?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, your testimony is correct, that this was at 8.00, not as the Prosecution suggested to you, 6.00.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct when I said that my statement given on the 13th is the most accurate one, and after my testimony I said that the time is not easy to remember, because the time span was really short and I couldn't remember it was 7.00 or 8.00. And my statement given on the 13th is probably the most accurate one because my memory was the freshest at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It was said that you had two interviews to -- with the investigators. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell us how the second interview ended?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we finished the second interview, I was told that I might be called once again to repeat certain events from that period and I should try and refresh my memory. That is what I was told. I was expecting to be -- expecting to be called, but I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: After the second interview, is this the next testimony which you're giving?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we exclude the meeting with you in the month of July, this is the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now could the witness be shown 1D24, page 3 in both the Macedonian and English versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recall that the Prosecution showed you this document?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLCE GROZDANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
